headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from ctx’s filesystem/MCP hooks paired with nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress; no direct pairwise docs, so uncertainty is elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, so attacker-controlled content can plausibly reach its instruction-processing path. nuwa-skill has network egress, creating a plausible bridge if ctx outputs are forwarded into B. No direct pairwise documentation exists, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ctx ingests untrusted file or tool output as instructions, injection is possible.
IF nuwa-skill consumes ctx-produced text without provenance checks, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of ctx-observed content as instructions.
Add a provenance tag to ctx outputs before passing them to nuwa-skill.
Restrict nuwa-skill to a read-only prompt template for ctx text.
Review any shared filesystem paths for untrusted artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, harness records, and filesystem content; nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or passes files between them, sensitive material from ctx can be exfiltrated by B’s outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ctx writes sensitive logs or graph data into a shared path, leakage becomes plausible.
IF nuwa-skill sends prompt or file contents over its allowlisted egress, those data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep ctx artifacts in a private directory not mounted into nuwa-skill.
Block nuwa-skill from reading ctx logs by default.
Redact audit/runtime logs before any handoff.
Limit nuwa-skill egress to known endpoints only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write to filesystem and run browsers, while nuwa-skill only advertises allowlisted network egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so a direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because ctx supports multiple instances and no locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable state without locks, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files.
Serialize any handoff that mutates state.
Check for lock support in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add explicit coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can emit logs and graph data that nuwa-skill could treat as input, but the profiles do not show either agent automatically acting on the other’s output. Because nuwa-skill has network egress, a mistaken assumption could propagate outward if the handoff is unverified. The lack of documented verification keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill treats ctx output as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade.
IF ctx-generated facts are forwarded into networked actions, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require a human review step before forwarding ctx output.
Add schema validation to ctx-to-nuwa handoffs.
Mark ctx outputs as untrusted by default.
Log provenance for every forwarded artifact.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, which can create retention or residency obligations, while nuwa-skill’s profile does not specify such data classes or compliance constraints. No direct mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance-gap risk is visible from the profiles.
conditions: IF ctx logs contain regulated data and are retained longer than policy allows, compliance risk appears.
IF nuwa-skill receives those logs without matching retention controls, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify ctx logs before sharing.
Set a short retention window for shared artifacts.
Exclude regulated fields from handoffs.
Review residency requirements for any exported logs.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
